ajad-p01-v01.speaker: pūrvapakṣin (Vijñānavādin)
ajad-p01-v01.question: What in things themselves distinguishes real from unreal, conscious from unconscious?
premises: Real and unreal show no difference in their own self (nijātmani).
Inert and non-inert likewise show none.
Hence the certainty: no distinguishing mark sits in the thing itself.
ajad-p01-v01.inference: The opponent's opening certainty: distinctions have no seat in things themselves.
uncertainties: Scope of the collapse (all things, or only cognized ones) stays open; vv2-8 grant it arguendo.

ajad-p01-v02.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
ajad-p01-v02.question: Do appearing, describing, or being touch a thing's essence?
premises: Showing (prakhyā), telling (upākhyā), being, and non-being its reverse contact nothing of own-form.
Own-form faces the knower alone (jñātṛgāmin); Vṛ: showing and kin are the knower's property (jñātur dharmas).

option_choices.reason: adas is distal (vs proximal idam); Vṛ glosses the referent with tat-, confirming the essence stands at arm's length.

ajad-p01-v03.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
ajad-p01-v03.question: Can a thing's own self consist in being-an-object-of-appearing?
premises: Object-of-appearing status leans on another (parāpekṣitayā).
What leans so keeps no single form (naikarūpatva).
It oversteps being itself (sattvalaṅghanāt).
ajad-p01-v03.inference: Appearing-objecthood cannot be a thing's self: dependence, formlessness, and excess rule it out.

ajad-p01-v04.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
ajad-p01-v04.question: Granted no difference — does the dispute collapse?
premises: Let distinction be denied outright (mā bhūd).
Still, from appearing's presence and absence a working difference succeeds (siddhyaty eva).
That much serves the end (prayojanam); Vṛ: function (arthakriyā) succeeds on that basis.
ajad-p01-v04.inference: Concession costs nothing: a purpose-serving difference survives the grant.
uncertainties: Whose purpose — the disputant's or the world's? Read as the opponent's own pragmatic end, per Vṛ's arthakriyā gloss.

ajad-p01-v05.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
ajad-p01-v05.question: What is being, cut loose from appearing?
premises: Being fits (ucitā) only as bound to appearing (avabhāsānuṣaktā).
Without that tie, existent and nonexistent stay undistinguished.
ajad-p01-v05.inference: Being is not free-standing; it is appearing-tied or nothing determinate.

ajad-p01-v06.speaker: objector (pāda ab), answered by Utpaladeva (pāda cd)
ajad-p01-v06.question: Does function (arthakriyā) distinguish existent from nonexistent?
premises: The existent alone works its function (arthakriyāṃ kuryāt); the other does not — so how undistinguished?
And yet the thing, in its own self (nijātmani), stays without mark.
Vṛ names the move: the objection (ākṣepa), then the reply — function runs on knowers (tattatpramātradhīnatayā), never self-seated.
ajad-p01-v06.inference: Function marks the scene, not the self: the objection states itself and is contained within the reply.

ajad-p01-v07.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
ajad-p01-v07.question: Does function-conditioned being escape the collapse?
premises: The existent arrives dyed with the qualifier 'appearing-as-functional' (arthakriyābhāsopādisaṃbhedam āgataḥ).
By own form it would subsist — yet nowise apart from the non-existent (nāsatas tu viśiṣyate).
Vṛ: grounded nowhere in awareness, the tint stays borrowed (upādhi).
ajad-p01-v07.inference: Borrowed dye is no distinction: conditioned being differs from non-being nowhere.

ajad-p01-v08.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
ajad-p01-v08.question: Is function at least what we declare of already-proven things?
premises: Of the thing with established being, no function is declared (na varṇitā).
Proven and unproven run exactly level (samam eva).
Hence (tena) all standing rests on awareness (pratiṣṭhā saṃvidāśrayā).
ajad-p01-v08.inference: First positive thesis: standing (pratiṣṭhā) is awareness-grounded, since function presupposes what it should prove.

ajad-p01-v09.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
ajad-p01-v09.question: Does bare, ungrasping awareness escape?
premises: Suppose awareness itself ungrasping-formed (aparāmarśarūpā).
Then it too, in itself, equals non-being and the inert (abhāvena jaḍena tulyā) — as before (prāgvat).
Vṛ: grasp-less shining, however world-illumining, is as dependent as crystal; the quietist Brahman-reading (śāntabrahmavāda) is glanced in refutation.
ajad-p01-v09.inference: The turn: grasp-less light is inert; only self-reflective awareness can ground.

ajad-p02-v10.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
ajad-p02-v10.question: Can the ungrounded ground another?
premises: She — grasp-less awareness, the subject carried over from v9 — stands unwon in finality (alabdhapariniṣṭhitiḥ) even by her become self (bhūtātmanā, svena).
How then would she go to standing-placehood (pratiṣṭhāspadatām iyāt) for another's being?
Vṛ: ungrounded awareness cannot settle another, as sky-flower yields no scent.
ajad-p02-v10.inference: The unself-grounded grounds nothing: v9's inert light cannot found another being.

ajad-p02-v11.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
ajad-p02-v11.question: How does consciousness take on grounding?
premises: Consciousness, apt (ucita) to ground another thing's showing by saying 'this' (idam iti).
And again, by itself (ātmanā), by saying 'I' (aham iti).
Vṛ: the split thing merits showing through this-grasp, then settlement through I-grasp; without rest in I, nothing becomes usable (vyavahārya).
ajad-p02-v11.inference: Consciousness fits itself to both poles: 'this' for the other's showing, 'I' for itself.

ajad-p02-v12.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
ajad-p02-v12.question: What orders the inert selves?
premises: By exclusion and inclusion (vyatireketarābhyām — Vṛ: anvayavyatirekābhyām, double concomitance) certainty (niścayaḥ) is called fixed-order, foundation, attainment, completion.
Of the other inert selves (anyajaḍātmanoḥ).
Vṛ: knower settled, the inert stands otherwise; self-and-other certainty runs on presence-and-absence.
ajad-p02-v12.inference: Certainty's four offices — order, ground, winning, winding-up — govern inert selves through double concomitance.

ajad-p02-v13.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
ajad-p02-v13.question: What being have inert things?
premises: In self near-unreal (asatkalpāḥ), these inert ones belong to shining alone (prakāśasyaiva).
Shining alone is — of own self, through selves own and other (svaparātmabhiḥ).
Vṛ: without rest in awareness they are near-unreal; shining alone swells, non-separate from its form, in both knower-known heaps — the autonomy-teaching (svātantryavāda) dawns here.
ajad-p02-v13.inference: Inert things have only borrowed being: shining alone is, owning both heaps — autonomy's first dawn.

ajad-p02-v14.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
ajad-p02-v14.question: Is there experience without grasp?
premises: No experience (anubhavaḥ) stands apart from distinct-and-indistinct certainty (bhinnābhinnaviniścayam).
None apart from connected shining, grasp-less in its self (vimarśarahitātmanaḥ).

Vṛ: cut from joining-severing autonomy, dull shining yields no relish-experience (saṃrambhātmānubhava); grasp's greatness is housing the world inside as self-one, then outshining it as this, then resting it in full I.
ajad-p02-v14.inference: Experience just is grasping certainty; grasp-less shining experiences nothing.

ajad-p02-v15.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
ajad-p02-v15.question: Where does cut-off 'this'-grasping complete?
premises: For this 'this'-grasping cut off (vicchinnavimarśasya), fulfillment (kṛtārthatā) is rest in own form (svasvarūpe viśrāntiḥ).
And that grasping — 'I am this' (so 'ham ity ayam) — is this itself.
Vṛ: the life-principle (jīvitasthānīya) — through it even inert stuff, one with the grasper-self, comes to rest as I; the non-inert are in truth one with the higher knower.
ajad-p02-v15.inference: Severed grasping completes in self-rest — 'I am this,' the done-ness that quickens even the inert.

ajad-p02-v16.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
ajad-p02-v16.question: How is the self both bound and free?
premises: The same self (sa eṣa evātmā) twofold: measured (mitaḥ) and unmeasured (aparimitaḥ).
Breath-bound (prāṇādinā niruddhaḥ): atom (aṇuḥ); as supreme self: unbroken (akhaṇḍitaḥ).
Vṛ: the Lord Himself, longing to sport the world-play, shows as breath-selves and contracts into living; uncontracted, He stays full, free awareness-self.
ajad-p02-v16.inference: One self, two measures — contracted atom, unbroken whole: play (krīḍā), not split.

ajad-p02-v17.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
ajad-p02-v17.question: What holds both measures?
premises: For both, this (eṣaḥ) is the end-ground (paryantabhūmiḥ) of all object-awarenesses (sarvārthasaṃvidām).
One alone (eka eva) through continuity (anusaṃdhānāt) — before-after joining makes flashing one.
So no other is possible (ato 'nyo nopapadyate).
Vṛ: resting-seat of all being-and-non-being awarenesses; difference cannot hold.
ajad-p02-v17.inference: Continuity alone gathers both measures into one end-ground; no second stands.

ajad-p02-v18.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
ajad-p02-v18.question: What shows at the limit?
premises: In I-knowing (ahaṃvidi) whose self is non-separation grasp (avyatirekātma-vimarśātman), limit-dwelling (paryantavartinyām).
Nothing inert beyond shining (bhāsanād adhikaṃ jaḍam) appears (bhāti).

Vṛ: in I-light non-separate from the world — seat of all knowing — the inert has no being past shining's measure; the lone non-inert knower flashes, never fallen from self-seat, outshining and reabsorbing the world-heap.
ajad-p02-v18.inference: Seal of the passage: at the limit, shining exhausts the inert; one knower flashes, world outshone and reabsorbed.

ajad-p03-v19.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
ajad-p03-v19.question: Can breath and kin be the knower?
premises: Though joined (samavāyin) with knowing and the rest, breath-and-kin are never proved (na siddhaḥ) by non-spreading (aprathana).
They would be knowables (prameyam), never knower (pramātā) — otherwise, delusion (anyato bhramāt).
Vṛ: the measured knower, joined with knowing-qualities, still fails by grasp-lack; grasp-lessness means inertia-compatriot; the breath-cage's knowability is borrowed error.
ajad-p03-v19.inference: Breath is demoted to knowable: the knower cannot be what never spreads.

ajad-p03-v20.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
ajad-p03-v20.question: Does the confined order escape the self?
premises: Though thing-abiding stands locked in the living (jīve niruddhā), curbed by breath and the eightfold city (prāṇapuryaṣṭakaniyantrite).
Even there, it abides (sthitā) in the supreme self (paramātmani).

Vṛ: in transactional living, all outer-inner order is curbed in contracted living — yet by contraction-lifting, as one with the higher knower, it stands in Śiva-self alone, since breath is non-separate from awareness-shine.
ajad-p03-v20.inference: Confinement is rehoused: even locked order abides in the supreme self.

ajad-p03-v21.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
ajad-p03-v21.question: Can breath restrain that self-nature?
premises: How (katham) could restraint (yantraṇā) by breath of him, of that self (tadātmana), ever be proved (sādhitā) — in recognition (pratyabhijñāyām)?
By living-ness (jīvatā), beyond non-showing (akhyāteḥ param).

Vṛ: how could breath-knowers veil unbroken full-I-flashing Śiva? Bondage is just unspreading of boundless power — called living-ness — settled at length in the Īśvarapratyabhijñā; discriminate thence.
ajad-p03-v21.inference: Breath-restraint is unprovable; living-ness outlies non-showing — recognition, not breath, settles it.
uncertainties: sādhitā's scope parsed with the Vṛ: restraint unprovable (kathaṃ), living-ness beyond non-showing — the nominal close read as verdict, not afterthought.

ajad-p03-v22.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
ajad-p03-v22.question: Where lies the ordering of things?
premises: No thing-ordering (nārthavyavasthā) lies in breath-and-kin through I-blocking (ahaṃbhāvanirodhataḥ).
Shining's self-rest (prakāśasyātmaviśrāntiḥ) is sung (kīrtitaḥ) as I-ness (ahaṃbhāvaḥ) — indeed (hi).
Vṛ: blocking the grasp (parāmarśa) that is mere self-shining, no thing-order holds, since order rests in awareness; self-rest of awareness is full-I-grasp by nature — the thing-orderer is sung.
ajad-p03-v22.inference: Order is not in breath but in I-ness: shining's self-rest, sung as the orderer.

ajad-p03-v23.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
ajad-p03-v23.question: What unfolds from rest?
premises: Told already (uktā): that rest (sā eva viśrāntiḥ — feminine, resumed) by blocking of all dependence (sarvāpekṣānirodhataḥ).
Freedom (svātantryam), then doership (kartṛtvaṃ) foremost (mukhyam), and lordship (īśvaratā) with it.
Vṛ: that same rest — end-ground of world-things' final standing — is freedom (needing no kit beyond itself), foremost doership, and the lordship the āgamas trumpet.
ajad-p03-v23.inference: Rest unfolds: freedom, then doership, then lordship — the absolute's offices from dependence-blocked rest.

ajad-p03-v24.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
ajad-p03-v24.question: Whence Māyā and world-making?
premises: Called Māyā (māyābhidāḥ), of his power alone (tacchakter eva — tat+śakteḥ, Vṛ: Śiva's power).
With no other proven (cānyāprasiddhitaḥ — ca+anyā+prasiddhitaḥ, Vṛ: no separate cause established, difference-identity vikalpa-felled).
This world-maker lordship (jagannirmātṛteśitā) is made of non-showing (tadakhyātimayam).
Vṛ: Māyā is Śiva's non-separate power, concealment-play; from that cause alone this non-showing-made world shines; world-shines' makerhood is lordship.
ajad-p03-v24.inference: Māyā from power alone, lordship from non-showing: no second cause survives.

ajad-p03-v25.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
ajad-p03-v25.question: What is proclaimed through linking?
premises: One alone (ekaiva) through linking (anusaṃdhānāt), she (sā) is proclaimed (proktā).
Of all awarenesses (sarvasaṃvidām): the mother-principle (mātṛtattvam), self-feeling's synonym (svasaṃvedanaparyāya), beginningless (anādi).
Vṛ: the sovereign higher power — linking severed blue-etc. awarenesses across before-after ends — one alone, grounding them, bounding them: the mother's beginningless principle.
ajad-p03-v25.inference: Proclamation: one linking mother-principle of all awarenesses, self-feeling itself, beginningless.

ajad-p03-v26.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
ajad-p03-v26.question: What fits the inert?
premises: Whatever grounding (niṣṭhā) of thing-ordering (bhāvavyavasthā) — pervasion (vyāpitvam) and linking (anusaṃdhānam) of the I-sharing him (tasyāhaṃbhāvabhāginaḥ).
That (taj) fits (yujyate) nothing inert (jaḍasya na).
Vṛ: where all things stand settled — awareness-self of full-I-grasp pith, freedom-never-parted — pervasion-as-linking holds everywhere; the unfree inert, grasp-pith-less, cannot host it.
ajad-p03-v26.inference: Pervasion and linking belong to I-sharers only: the inert cannot host them.

ajad-p03-v27.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddhāntin)
ajad-p03-v27.question: What is the verdict?
premises: So (tatas) within difference (bhede), shining's shining (bhāsasya bhāsamānatā) holds good (ghaṭate).
Hence (tena) said (uktam) in recognition (pratyabhijñāyām): this world (jagat) is that-nondual-made (tadadvayamayaṃ).

Vṛ: holding to non-inertness — in this difference-flashing world, blue-pleasure-etc. shining keeps unspent inward seat while outshining through knowing-power (hence shining-shining holds); holding to non-difference, the inert re-shines — else unshining. So in the glorious Īśvarapratyabhijñā the world is said awareness-nondual-natured. Peace (iti śivam).
ajad-p03-v27.inference: Verdict: difference keeps shining-shining; recognition says the world that-nondual-made.

ajad-p01-v01.plain_english: Just as there is no difference between the real and the unreal in their own nature, so too — this is certain — there is no such difference between the inert and the non-inert.
ajad-p01-v01.sanskrit_cite: yathā sadasatām naiva viśeṣo 'sti nijātmani jadājaḍānām apy evaṃ nāsty asāv iti niścayaḥ

ajad-p01-v02.plain_english: Appearing (prakhyā) and describing (upākhyā), existence and its opposite, non-existence — none of this touches a thing's essence; that essence is what faces the knower.
ajad-p01-v02.sanskrit_cite: prakhyopākhyā ca sattā yad yad asattā viparyayaḥ naitat svarūpaṃ spṛśati vastuno jñātṛgāmy adaḥ

ajad-p01-v03.plain_english: Nor can a thing's very self be "being an object of appearing and describing" — for that would make it depend on something else, give it no single form, and break past existence itself.
ajad-p01-v03.sanskrit_cite: prakhyopākhyāviṣayatāpy arthasyātmā na yujyate parāpekṣitayā naikarūpatve sattvalaṅghanāt

ajad-p01-v04.plain_english: Granted, let there be no difference; still, from the presence and absence of appearing, a difference does get established here — and that much serves the purpose.
ajad-p01-v04.sanskrit_cite: mā bhūd viśeṣaḥ prakhyādibhāvābhāvau tataḥ punaḥ siddhyaty eva viśeṣo 'tra tāvatā ca prayojanam

ajad-p01-v05.plain_english: Even so, existence would only be fitting as tied to appearing; without reference to that, existent and nonexistent are indistinguishable.
ajad-p01-v05.sanskrit_cite: evam apy avabhāsānuṣaktā sattocitā bhavet tadapekṣāṃ vinā bhāvābhāvayor aviśiṣṭatā

ajad-p01-v06.plain_english: But how could they be indistinguishable here, when the existent performs a function (arthakriyā) and the other does not? And yet the thing, in its own self, remains without distinction.
ajad-p01-v06.sanskrit_cite: kathaṃ syād aviśeṣo 'tra yāvatārthakriyāṃ hi san kuryān nānyas tathāpy artho nirviśeṣo nijātmani

ajad-p01-v07.plain_english: So the existent thing, having taken on the limiting condition of appearing-as-functional, would exist by its own essence — yet it is not distinguished from the nonexistent.
ajad-p01-v07.sanskrit_cite: evam arthakriyābhāsopādhisaṃbhedam āgataḥ sann arthaḥ syāt svarūpeṇa nāsatas tu viśiṣyate

ajad-p01-v08.plain_english: But even there, function is not what is described in a thing whose existence is already established; the two are exactly on par — hence their grounding rests on consciousness.
ajad-p01-v08.sanskrit_cite: tatrāpy arthakriyā siddhasattākārthe na varṇitā samam evānayos tena pratiṣṭhā saṃvidāśrayā

ajad-p01-v09.plain_english: And if consciousness itself were of the form of non-grasping (aparāmarśa), then it too, in itself, would be exactly equal to the inert non-being, as before.
ajad-p01-v09.sanskrit_cite: saṃvid apy aparāmarśarūpā cet tad asāv api abhāvena jaḍenātha tulyaiva prāgvad ātmani

ajad-p02-v10.plain_english: If she — by her become self-nature — has never won final grounding, how could she become the standing-place of establishment for another existent?
ajad-p02-v10.sanskrit_cite: saivaṃ bhūtātmanā svenāpy alabdhapariniṣṭhitiḥ katham anyasya bhāvasya pratiṣṭhāspadatām iyāt

ajad-p02-v11.plain_english: Consciousness, apt to ground another thing's showing by saying 'this,' would take that grounding nature — and again, by itself, by saying 'I.'
ajad-p02-v11.sanskrit_cite: idam ity ucitaḥ saṃvit prakāśe 'nyasya vastunaḥ pratiṣṭhātmakatāṃ gacched aham ity ātmanā punaḥ

ajad-p02-v12.plain_english: For certainty — by exclusion and inclusion both — is called the fixed order, the foundation, the attainment, the completion of the other, inert selves.
ajad-p02-v12.sanskrit_cite: vyatireketarābhyām hi niścayo 'nyajaḍātmanoḥ vyavasthitiḥ pratiṣṭhā ca siddhir nirvṛttir ucyate

ajad-p02-v13.plain_english: So these inert ones, near-unreal in themselves, belong to shining alone; shining alone is — of its own self, through selves both own and other.
ajad-p02-v13.sanskrit_cite: evam ātmany asatkalpāḥ prakāśasyaiva santy amī jaḍāḥ prakāśa evāsti svātmanaḥ svaparātmabhiḥ

ajad-p02-v14.plain_english: And there is no experience apart from distinct-and-indistinct certainty — apart from connected shining, grasp-less in its self.
ajad-p02-v14.sanskrit_cite: na caivānubhavo 'py asti bhinnābhinnaviniścayam muktvānvayasya prakāśasya vimarśarahitātmanaḥ

ajad-p02-v15.plain_english: For this 'this'-grasping, cut off, fulfillment is rest in its own form — and that grasping, 'I am this,' is this itself.
ajad-p02-v15.sanskrit_cite: idam ity asya vicchinnavimarśasya kṛtārthatā yā svasvarūpe viśrāntir vimarśaḥ so 'ham ity ayam

ajad-p02-v16.plain_english: Twofold is this same self: measured and unmeasured — by breath and the rest restrained, an atom; as supreme self, unbroken.
ajad-p02-v16.sanskrit_cite: dvidhā sa eṣa evātmā mito 'parimitas tathā prāṇādinā niruddho 'ṇuḥ paramātmā tv akhaṇḍitaḥ

ajad-p02-v17.plain_english: For both, this is the end-ground of all object-awarenesses — one alone through continuity. So no other is possible.
ajad-p02-v17.sanskrit_cite: ubhayo 'py eṣa paryantabhūmiḥ sarvārthasaṃvidām eka evānusandhānād ato 'nyo nopapadyate

ajad-p02-v18.plain_english: And in the I-knowing whose self is non-separation grasp, limit-dwelling — nothing inert beyond shining appears.
ajad-p02-v18.sanskrit_cite: na cāpy avyatirekātmavimarśātmany ahaṃvidi bhāti paryantavartinyāṃ bhāsanād adhikaṃ jaḍam

ajad-p03-v19.plain_english: Never proved by non-spreading — though joined with knowing and the rest — breath and kin would be knowables, never knowers. Otherwise, delusion.
ajad-p03-v19.sanskrit_cite: na siddho 'prathanād eva jñānādisamavāyy api tat prāṇādi prameyaṃ syān na pramātānyato bhramāt

ajad-p03-v20.plain_english: Though the abiding of things stands locked in the living, curbed by breath and the eightfold city — even there, in the supreme self it abides.
ajad-p03-v20.sanskrit_cite: yady apy arthasthitiḥ prāṇapuryaṣṭakaniyantrite jīve niruddhā tatrāpi paramātmani sā sthitā

ajad-p03-v21.plain_english: How could restraint by breath of that self-nature ever be proved — in recognition? By living-ness, beyond non-showing.
ajad-p03-v21.sanskrit_cite: tadātmanaiva tasya syāt kathaṃ prāṇena yantraṇā sādhitā pratyabhijñāyām akhyāter jīvatā param

ajad-p03-v22.plain_english: No ordering of things lies in breath and the rest through blocking of I-ness; shining's self-rest is sung as I-ness, indeed.
ajad-p03-v22.sanskrit_cite: nārthavyavasthā prāṇādāv ahaṃbhāvanirodhataḥ prakāśasyātmaviśrāntir ahaṃbhāvo hi kīrtitaḥ

ajad-p03-v23.plain_english: Told already — that very rest, by blocking of all dependence: freedom, then doership foremost, and lordship too.
ajad-p03-v23.sanskrit_cite: uktā saiva ca viśrāntiḥ sarvāpekṣānirodhataḥ svātantryam atha kartṛtvaṃ mukhyam īśvaratāpi ca

ajad-p03-v24.plain_english: Called Māyā, of his power alone — with no other proven; this world-maker lordship is made of non-showing.
ajad-p03-v24.sanskrit_cite: māyābhidās tacchakter eva cānyāprasiddhitaḥ tadakhyātimayaṃ hy etaj jagannirmātṛteśitā

ajad-p03-v25.plain_english: One alone through linking, proclaimed: of all awarenesses the mother-principle, self-feeling's synonym — beginningless.
ajad-p03-v25.sanskrit_cite: ekaiva cānusaṃdhānāt sā proktā sarvasaṃvidām svasaṃvedanaparyāyamātṛtattvam anādi tat

ajad-p03-v26.plain_english: Whatever grounds the ordering of things — pervasion and linking of the I-sharer — fits nothing inert.
ajad-p03-v26.sanskrit_cite: bhāvavyavasthā yan niṣṭhā tasyāhaṃbhāvabhāginaḥ vyāpitvam anusaṃdhānaṃ taj jaḍasya na yujyate

ajad-p03-v27.plain_english: So within difference, shining's shining holds good — hence recognition's word: this world is that-nondual-made.
ajad-p03-v27.sanskrit_cite: tato bhede tu bhāsasya ghaṭate bhāsamānatā tenoktam pratyabhijñāyāṃ tadadvayamayaṃ jagat

essence: Every candidate seat of distinction — predicates, objecthood, conceded difference, free-standing being, function — collapses into knower-dependence; the opponent's no-difference is granted, then outflanked from inside (vv1-8).
Grasping-less awareness is declared inert, and the proof turns: only self-reflective consciousness can stand as ground (v9).

sections.SUMMARY: Real and unreal differ nowhere in their own self — the opponent's certainty, stretched to conscious and unconscious. Showing, telling, being: none of it touches own-form, which faces the knower alone. Object-of-showing fits no self, since leaning breaks oneness and oversteps being. The grant costs nothing — appearing's coming and going still serves the end. Being fits only appearing-bound. Function cannot part them either: only existents work, yet working leans on knowers. So all standing is awareness-based. And awareness itself, ungrasping-formed, ranks with non-being and the inert.
sections.FUNCTION: Opens the Siddhitrayī's second proof with the opponent's strongest certainty, then dissolves every candidate seat of distinction from inside — landing awareness-grounded standing and the grasp-less turn.
sections.KEY TERMS: sadasat (real-unreal) · jaḍa/ajaḍa (inert/non-inert) · prakhyā/upākhyā (showing/telling) · jñātṛgāmin (knower-facing) · arthakriyā (working) · pratiṣṭhā (standing) · saṃvidāśrayā (awareness-grounded) · aparāmarśa (ungrasping) · vimarśa kept as grasping against the field's reflective awareness (grounds in NOTE)
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: Ajaḍapramātṛsiddhi, Utpaladeva (10th c.), mūla with his own vṛtti; GRETIL KSTS 34. Second proof of the Siddhitrayī. Passage 1 of 3: vv. 1–9. Vṛ read as Utpaladeva's own per the closing colophon (Harabhaṭṭa layer open — see NOTE).
sections.EXPLANATION: The opponent's certainty is granted, then each ground is removed: predicates never touch own-form; objecthood needs another, one form, being; concession still works; being apart from appearing is indeterminate; function marks the scene, not the self; dyed being is borrowed; proven things run level — so standing falls back on awareness. Then the turn: ungrasping awareness ranks inert.
sections.BOUNDARY: Whose end the conceded difference serves stays open. The Vṛ's quietist-Brahman glance recorded, not pressed. GRETIL dental-d quirk in jadājaḍānām read with the editions. adaḥ corrected distal at L0.

rasa.sthayibhava: vismaya (wonder) that awareness itself can rank inert
rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is the shock of the turn (v9): after eight verses of demolition, the proof stings its own ground — bare shining is jaḍa. The vyabhicāri is intellectual triumph (vīra) as each candidate dissolves. Abhinava's camatkāra covers dispute-relish: wonder at reasoning that unseats its own seat.

essence: What never stood cannot stand another: consciousness fits itself to this and I, orders inert selves by double certainty, and completes severed grasping in self-rest (vv10-15).
The same self twofold — breath-bound atom, unbroken whole — gathers in one continuous end-ground where nothing shows more inert than shining (vv16-18).

sections.SUMMARY: What never stood cannot stand another: unwon herself, grasp-less awareness grounds no other being. Consciousness fits to ground another's showing by saying this — and again, itself, by saying I. By exclusion and inclusion both, certainty orders inert selves: fixed order, ground, winning, winding-up. Near-unreal in self, inert ones are shining's own; shining alone is, through selves own and other. No experience stands apart from distinct-and-indistinct assurance, apart from linked ungrasping shining. Cut-off this-grasping completes in self-rest: I-am-this is this. One self twofold — breath-bound atom, unbroken whole. Both gather in one end-ground through linking alone. At the limit, in no-parting I-knowing, nothing shows more inert than shining.
sections.FUNCTION: Builds the positive account after the demolition: self-grounding first, then the two sayings, certainty's offices, borrowed being, grasp as experience, completion in rest, the twofold one, the gathering, the seal.
sections.KEY TERMS: pratiṣṭhāspadatā (standing-placehood) · idam/aham (this/I) · vyatireka/itara (exclusion/inclusion) · asatkalpa (near-unreal) · anusaṃdhāna (linking) · paryantabhūmi (end-ground) · ahaṃvid (I-knowing) · vimarśa kept as grasping (see p01 NOTE)
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: Passage 2 of 3: vv. 10–18. The knower must first ground itself. Vṛ read as Utpaladeva's own (authorship open — see p01 NOTE).
sections.EXPLANATION: Self-grounding preconditions all grounding; two sayings, two poles; certainty's four offices with double concomitance; inert being as borrowed shining with autonomy dawning inside; experience identified with grasping; severed grasping completed in rest; one self shown twofold; gathered by linking; sealed at the limit.
sections.BOUNDARY: Feminine subject kept (she). itara read as anvaya side with the Vṛ. No live token forks in this passage.

rasa.sthayibhava: śama (settling) as self-rest completing severed grasping
rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is rest itself (viśrānti, kṛtārthatā): the passage lands twice in settling — grasping completed (v15), both measures gathered (v17). The vyabhicāri is wonder at the twofold one (v16): atom and unbroken, same self. Abhinava's śānta as the relish of recognition completed — homecoming after demolition.

essence: Breath, body, and the eightfold city are demoted to knowables: no ordering lies in breath, no restraint touches the self, and living-ness stands beyond non-showing (vv19-22).

Rest unfolds into freedom, doership, lordship; Māyā named from power alone; the beginningless mother-principle proclaimed; pervasion fenced to I-sharers; the world verdict that-nondual-made (vv23-27).

sections.SUMMARY: Breath joined with knowing still never proves: breath and kin are knowables, never knowers — else delusion. Locked in the living though things stand, curbed by breath and eightfold city, even there they abide in the supreme self. Breath proves no hold on that self-nature; recognition answers by living-ness past non-showing. No ordering sits in breath by I-blocking; shining's self-rest is sung as I-ness. Told already, that rest, all dependence blocked: freedom, doership foremost, lordship with it. Called Māyā, of his power alone, no other proven — world-maker lordship is non-showing-made. One alone through linking, proclaimed mother-principle of all awarenesses, self-feeling's synonym, beginningless. Pervasion and linking of the I-sharer fit nothing inert. So in difference shining's shining holds — recognition's word: this world that-nondual-made.
sections.FUNCTION: Closes by elimination then proclamation: breath demoted, confinement rehoused, restraint unproved, order relocated — then rest unfolded, Māyā named, the mother proclaimed, pervasion fenced, verdict spoken.
sections.KEY TERMS: prameya/pramātṛ (knowable/knower) · puryaṣṭaka (eightfold city) · akhyāti (non-showing) · ahaṃbhāva (I-ness) · viśrānti (rest) · svātantrya/kartṛtva/īśvaratā (freedom/doership/lordship) · māyā (Māyā) · mātṛtattva (mother-principle) · tadadvayamaya (that-nondual-made)
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: Passage 3 of 3: vv. 19–27. Elimination complete, proclamation begins. Closes with iti śivam; Harabhaṭṭa colophon paratext.
sections.EXPLANATION: Breath fails despite knowings; locked order rehoused; restraint unprovable; ordering moved to I-ness. Rest opens into three offices; Māyā from power alone; one linking mother proclaimed; pervasion fenced; verdict keeps difference and non-difference, speaking the world nondual.
sections.BOUNDARY: sādhitā's scope held open as reading. śaiva ghost exorcised by feminine anaphora. v25 compound listed, not split. v27 double holding kept double. iti śivam and colophons excluded.

rasa.sthayibhava: utsāha (exultation) as verdict-joy in proclaiming the close
rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is exultation: four verbs of proclaiming — sung (v22), told (v23), proclaimed (v25), said (v27) — carry the passage to its verdict.
